# ⚡ Quick Rules — the 60-second read

Read this digest every run; open the numbered lesson in the table below only when a rule bites. **Brain hygiene:** the hub is Snapshot-first and append-never — rewrite the 📸 Snapshot in place, create ALL dated pages inside 🗄️ Logs & Archive, park ideas in 💡 Ideas & Research; if the hub exceeds ~2 phone screens, something is misplaced.

**Before you act (every session)**

- Reconcile any brain claim about branches/PRs against LIVE git before acting on it (#10, #32).
- Preflight push credentials decisively: `env | grep -i token`, `git config credential.helper`, `~/.git-credentials`, `grep 'x-access-token' /tmp/*/.git/config`; one-shot proof `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 git ls-remote <PRIVATE repo>` (#11, #12, #19, #28).
- Preflight REST access, don't assume: only the Cowork sandbox blocks `api.github.com`; mobile/web/Code sessions usually have it — `curl` the `/user` endpoint with the PAT (#2, #31).
- New feature build → check the 🔗 Work Claims Ledger AND grep for a same-purpose module first (#16, #20).
- Unfamiliar repo → grep once for committed `<<<<<<<` conflict markers (#15).
- Setting a project's next task → check it against the Decisions page and merged-PR rationale first; don't queue work that re-opens a settled decision (#33).
- Verify EVERY project's repo each sweep, not just the ones with recent brain activity — low-priority projects hide drift longest, a ls-remote/shallow-clone is seconds (#46).
**Shipping (the claude/** auto-merge pipeline)

- Auth as `x-access-token:<TOKEN>@github.com`, never `username:<TOKEN>` (#1).
- Don't assume the auto-merge pipeline file is literally named `auto-merge.yml` — list `.github/workflows/` and read each file's triggers; bussnessbuilder uses `workforce-merge.yml` (#45).
- PR code scope, head SHA, and open/merge state are readable via `refs/pull/N/head` / `refs/pull/N/merge` without REST — only the PR body text needs REST (#39).
- `git cherry` only proves patch-identical merges, not "not superseded" — before calling a cherry-flagged branch real unmerged work, also match its commit message against a merged `(#N)` title and grep main for the feature's files (#47).
- A push to `claude/**` is an atomic, FINAL handoff: batch commits, push ONCE per task — a second push races the pipeline and orphans commits (#25, #30).
- Confirm every push with `git ls-remote`; confirm a commit actually reached main with `git branch -r --contains <sha>` — a deleted branch is not proof of a merge (#4, #29, #30).
- Never stack on unmerged branches; merge bottom-first (#5).
- Recovered/old branch → check for a stale base (`git diff --stat main..<branch>`), cherry-pick onto current main, never raw-push (#26).
- "CI is green" needs the PR's actual check runs, not repo workflow history (#24); a green pipeline run is NOT a drained queue — conflicts skip silently (#29).
- "No open PR" + surviving branch ref ≠ stranded work: prove unmerged-ness with `git cherry origin/main origin/<branch>` before re-triggering anything (#32).
- After a shared fix lands on main, explicitly merge main into each open sibling branch — rerun-failed-jobs uses the stale snapshot (#13).
**Verifying (honesty gate)**

- A brain note claiming "tsc clean"/"build green" is not proof — pull the PR's real check runs and read the failing job's log before building on top (#40).
- Verifying every project "cheaply"? Still touch EVERY repo's live git state (a shallow clone/ls-remote is seconds) — low-priority projects are where brain-vs-reality drift hides longest and goes unnoticed for days (#46).
- Done = symptom proven gone (reproduce → fix → prove); label the verification level; never claim an unproven push/merge/delete (#4, #21, #29).
- No "verified" claim without a committed test-file path (#21).
- Zero conflict markers ≠ correct resolution — rebuild/typecheck after every conflict resolution (#14).
- Sandbox toolchains are flaky: ≤2 install attempts, then verify what you CAN (`node --check`, per-file esbuild transpile, tsc filtered to your files) and rely on the CI gate (#17, #22, #27).
**When stuck**

- Loop-breaker: same failure ~2× → change approach or escalate (#3, #6).
- No filler work; queue empty → stop and say so (#7). Complex planning uses the top model (#8).
- Outputs folders are ephemeral — persist to Notion or a pushed branch; a patch page is a fallback, the real commit is better (#9, #26).
- Notion won't load / brain outage → session-level tool gap, not an auth problem; don't loop re-authing. Do the work, keep a durable record, and run a catch-up sync on the first reconnected session (#34).
**Writing code that actually runs (#59–#76)**

- **The dominant defect in HomeBot is a capability nothing can reach.** Six instances in one day: a threshold excluding every real value, a logger with no caller, a cap set below the set it bounds, a tool missing from an allowlist while the prompt promised it, an intent with no routing pattern, an export wired to nothing. All passed every test. After building any capability, prove the PATH: does a real request reach it? (#66, #69, #73)
- A bounds test passes hardest when the feature is OFF. Pair every limit test with a liveness test asserting the feature DOES something. Delete tautology tests (`expect(MAX).toBe(12)`) — they only ever block the fix (#69).
- When two constants must relate (a cap and the size of what it bounds), assert the RELATION — they live in different declarations and nothing else compares them (#69).
- **A/B every gate: revert the fix and watch the test fail.** Print proof the mutation applied first. "Still passes with the fix removed" is a finding about the CLAIM, not a flaky run (#70).
- A mock encodes someone else's contract and silently rots. For any external service or binary, write ONE opt-in live test (env-gated, out of CI) and run it before building on top (#73).
- `e.message` is optional — not everything thrown is an Error (#73).
- A pinned dependency several majors behind may be failing on an upstream auth/protocol change, not your code (#73).
**Before escalating or claiming (#67, #74)**

- Before telling Aden something needs his decision, credential, or library — GREP FOR IT. Asking him to choose what the repo already ships reads as not having looked (#74).
- Before reporting a defect, check REACHABILITY: is the broken path even executable? Two "bugs" this session were unreachable code (#74).
- A model's audit of its own config is indicative, not authoritative — but a wrong diagnosis can carry a right observation. Verify each claim, then say plainly which held (#67).
**Mechanics that keep biting**

- If content contains a backtick, `${`, a backslash, or a regex: DO NOT put it in a shell one-liner. Use the exact-match editor or a script file. This is mechanical, not a judgement call — it recurred 5× in one day AFTER being recorded (#68, #75).
- Never `git checkout <file>` to undo an A/B mutation when that file also holds the fix (#75).
- Squash-merged commits reappear as add/add conflicts on a long-lived branch. Fix: `git rebase --onto origin/main <last-merged-sha> <branch>`. Better: one branch per self-contained change (#76).
- Same commit, different result in two places = runtime difference, not flakiness. Compare versions before touching code; read the failing job's LOG, not its name (#72).
- A permanently-red non-blocking check gets ignored, and its real signal with it. Make it required or delete it. Get the pass/fail COUNT before believing "everything is broken" (#71).

## 🔁 How this stays live

This page is only useful if the lessons get **used**, not just stored. The loop:

1. **Read first.** Every run reads the ⚡ Quick Rules digest before acting; open full rows as needed. The hub and the Manual Checklist both point here.
1. **Append on failure.** Every mistake or lesson learned = a new row at the bottom of the table (next number, date, lesson, rule, where it applies) before the session ends. A lesson that isn't written down will be relearned.
1. **Keep the digest in sync.** If a new lesson changes day-to-day behavior, add/adjust one line in ⚡ Quick Rules citing its number.
1. **Enforce + propagate weekly.** The weekly Brain Health task enforces these rules and propagates them into the scheduled-task run-prompts and each repo's `CLAUDE.md` Operating Rules (#23).
If you ever catch yourself about to do something this page warns against — stop. The cost of these lessons was already paid.

Copy this row format when adding a lesson (next number, never reuse one):

`| N | YYYY-MM-DD | what went wrong | the rule that prevents it | where it applies |`

### 🆕 Lesson #50 root cause — now confirmed (2026-07-06, same "what's next" session, continued)

Before writing "widget/ (or any dir) can't be verified in-sandbox", try `--ignore-scripts` + targeted per-package postinstall first. Extends #22/#27 (partial installs) and #38 (widget's commonjs quirk): the widget IS verifiable, just not via a plain `npm ci`. | Any in-sandbox verification of the SADIE widget/ dir, or any package whose default install is blocked only by a postinstall hitting a non-allowlisted host. |`

**#59 — Verify security-rule assumptions against real call sites before handing off (2026-07-09).** When drafting Firestore/security rules, don't ship a draft built on assumptions about the data model — read every actual read/write call site first. On shopFront, my first-draft lockdown *looked* correct but would have broken guest checkout: the owner-only `isSignedIn() && userId==uid` rule blocks a logged-out guest from reading their own booking back and updating it to `confirmed`, which is exactly what CheckoutPage does with no login. Only reading `BookingPage`/`CheckoutPage`/`ConfigContext` revealed (a) guest bookings use `userId:'guest'` and must be reachable by unguessable doc-id capability, (b) `siteSettings/integrations` is read unauthenticated at checkout so it can't be staff-only, and (c) a world-readable catch-all would expose that integrations doc — so once you've *enumerated every top-level collection* (here: services, addons, promoCodes, bookings, users, siteSettings), switch the catch-all to deny-by-default. Rule of thumb: a security rule you haven't traced against the app's real queries is as likely to break the app as to secure it. Enumerate collections → match each explicitly → deny the rest → leave emulator-testing + deploy to Aden (needs Firebase auth).

**#60 — Verify the actual clone path / $HOME before constructing absolute file paths (2026-07-09).** Building the SADIE permission audit/history feature, `create_file` was handed `/home/claude/work/sadie/...` on the assumption that the sandbox home was `/home/claude`. It isn't — `$HOME` is `/root`, and my `git clone` had landed the repo at `/root/work/sadie`. The file was created successfully into a *parallel* `/home/claude/...` tree that had nothing to do with the clone, so a following `str_replace` on the real file failed "File not found" until I noticed the mismatch and `mv`'d it across. Cost ~2 extra tool calls. Rule: before writing files with absolute paths in a fresh sandbox, confirm the real working dir once (`pwd`/`echo $HOME` — this sandbox is `/root`, not `/home/claude`), and prefer deriving paths from the actual clone dir (e.g. capture `REPO=$(pwd)` right after cloning) rather than assuming a home location. A create_file that "succeeds" is not proof it landed where your other edits are pointing. Applies to any session mixing `git clone` + create_file/str_replace with absolute paths.

**#61 — A repo's real CI runtime is a property of that repo, not a global auto-merge timing pattern (2026-07-10).** Pushed shootemup's `claude/gameconfig-bullet-offset-extraction` and it was still open ~75s later — under a naive read of lesson #42 ("PR outlives the merge timing already observed for its own sibling PRs") that could look stuck and tempt a direct force-merge. But shootemup's `android-ci.yml` runs a full Android build (SDK setup, `./gradlew test`, `./gradlew assembleDebug`) before `auto-merge.yml` even opens/merges the PR — a genuine multi-minute job, unlike the docs-only or lightweight-CI repos where lesson #42's ~10-20s pattern was actually observed (e.g. comand's WebGL PRs). Before judging a claude/** branch "stuck," skim that specific repo's own CI workflow steps once to know its real expected runtime — don't apply a portfolio-wide timing expectation, and don't force-merge or poll every 15s for minutes on a repo whose CI genuinely takes that long. Applies to: any repo where the claude/**-triggered CI does a real compiled-language build/test (Android/Gradle, iOS, native, etc.) rather than a fast script/lint pass.


# 2026-07-10 — Vacuum Empire device testing (Capacitor + Firebase on Android)

- **Firestore in a Capacitor Android WebView needs a special transport.** Plain `getFirestore()` leaves every listener permanently erroring (`WebChannelConnection RPC 'Listen' stream transport errored`). Fix: `initializeFirestore(app, { experimentalForceLongPolling: true, useFetchStreams: false } as any, databaseId)`. Force-long-polling alone was NOT enough — `useFetchStreams: false` was also required. Verified on device: errors gone.
- **`signInWithPopup`**** never works inside the Capacitor WebView** (button silently does nothing). Use `@capacitor-firebase/authentication` native plugin: add `FirebaseAuthentication: { skipNativeAuth: false, providers: ['google.com'] }` to `capacitor.config.ts` plugins (missing providers list gives "Google sign-in provider is not enabled"), register the debug SHA-1 in Firebase console, re-download `google-services.json` (must contain a `client_type: 1` oauth client — without it Credential Manager throws `NoCredentialException: No credentials available`).
- **Diagnose device issues from logcat, not guesses**: `adb logcat --pid=$(pidof <pkg>)` surfaced the exact plugin/Firestore errors each time. A 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` from a raw REST probe of Firestore proved backend/key/database were fine and isolated the fault to the WebView transport.
- **AI Studio re-exports clobber repo infrastructure.** The new gameplay drop on main deleted all 5 CI workflows, fastlane, the legal/privacy-policy pages, [CLAIMS.md](http://claims.md/), the release-signing gradle config, corrupted `gradle-wrapper.jar` (binary), renamed the appId to `com.vacuumempire.game`, and shipped a TS error (no CI left to catch it). When merging an AI-studio export: diff first, take gameplay only, restore infra from the previous branch, and keep the Firebase-registered appId (`com.kingithegreat.vacuumempire`) — renaming it silently breaks Google sign-in and the google-services check.
- **Firebase console setup for this project** (sitebuilder-b2ee6): Google + Anonymous providers must be enabled under Authentication → Sign-in method; debug SHA-1 `996443662518e1bec3010deccd2f8d6f350f70f5` is registered for `com.kingithegreat.vacuumempire`.
**Lesson (2026-07-26, Sadie n8n auth):** n8n's public REST API (`POST /api/v1/workflows`, `X-N8N-API-KEY`) rejects unknown top-level properties — strip workflow JSON to `name`/`nodes`/`connections`/`settings` before creating, and activate via `POST /workflows/{id}/activate` (registers webhooks live, no container restart). CLI fallback for activation is `n8n update:workflow --id=X --active=true`, never direct SQLite. Also: Sadie's widget jest suite has 7 pre-existing failing suites locally (electron `app.getPath` undefined in the jest env) — verify failures against a clean stash before attributing them to your diff.

**Lesson (2026-07-26, Sadie voice input):** When a feature is "broken", grep for a better implementation already sitting unwired in the repo before building from scratch — Sadie's mic button used legacy Windows SAPI dictation via PowerShell while a complete offline Whisper module (`speech/offline-recognition.ts`) existed as dead code, and `@huggingface/transformers` was already in package.json. The fix was wiring + settings, not a new dependency.

### 🆕 Lesson #60 (2026-08-10) — fold into the table at next Brain Health run

`| 60 | 2026-08-10 | Any transform that can meet its own output must be idempotent or it compounds. HomeBot encrypted API keys on save with no ciphertext marker, so every save re-encrypted the previous ciphertext (~33% growth per pass). Found in the wild as a user-settings.json whose apiKey was 180,106,622 characters — 180MB. Separately, corrupt-file recovery archived the bad file but left it in place, so every cache expiry re-archived it: 42 .corrupt-* copies stamped 30s apart. | Mark transformed values (enc:v1:) and make the transform a no-op on marked input; add a size cap on EVERY field of that class, not just the one that bloated last time. Recovery must leave the next read SUCCEEDING — archive once, then write the repaired file, and test by reading twice. | encryption, encoding, migration, any save/load round-trip |`

### 🆕 Lesson #62 (2026-08-10) — fold into the table at next Brain Health run

`| 62 | 2026-08-10 | Three bugs in a new subprocess provider were invisible to a green test suite and only appeared when the CLI was actually run: (a) spawn EINVAL — npm installs global CLIs as .cmd and modern Node refuses to spawn .cmd without shell:true (CVE-2024-27980); a sibling provider using a real .exe never hits this, so copying working code ships broken; (b) once shell:true is forced, argv is concatenated UNESCAPED, so a user prompt containing & or | would execute commands; (c) the CLI read stdin for extra context and hung forever, invisible from a terminal because the shell had already closed stdin. | For subprocess providers: pass untrusted input over STDIN, never argv; always child.stdin.end(); and verify by running the real binary through a throwaway script using the SAME spawn shape as production, A/B with and without the fix. A passing unit suite proves nothing about a subprocess. | any provider/tool that spawns an external binary, esp. on Windows |`

The existing suite asserted only that the result never EXCEEDS the cap — a permanently truncated list satisfies that perfectly — and also contained `expect(MAX_TOOLS).toBe(12)`, a tautology restating the constant that blocked the fix while protecting nothing. | Bounds tests must be paired with a liveness test: assert the feature DOES something (this input yields a tool of that category), not merely that it stays inside its limit. When two constants must relate (a cap and the size of what it bounds), assert the RELATION in a test — `expect(CORE.size).toBeLessThan(MAX)` — because the two numbers live in different declarations and nothing else compares them. ### 🆕 Lesson #76 (2026-08-12) — fold into the table at next Brain Health run

`| 76 | 2026-08-12 | A long-lived branch whose commits are squash-merged one at a time goes DIRTY repeatedly, and the conflict is a phantom. It happened three times in one session and a naive `git merge origin/main` would have produced duplicated diffs. | Recognise it by the shape: add/add conflicts on files you know are already on main. Extracting a video frame showed captions off the top of the screen that ffprobe called a valid file. Probing elementFromPoint showed the app header eating the Settings ✕ that CSS said was on top. n8n's own execution record named the 403 and quoted Wikipedia's robot policy. | Look at the output, not the source. Add a debug hook behind an env var and keep it — HOMEBOT_DEBUG_PROMPT is now permanent because it is what found the bug. Extract a frame, dump the request body, ask the DOM what is at that pixel, read the execution log. A theory about the code is a hypothesis; the artifact is evidence. | any bug where the code "looks correct" and the behaviour disagrees |`


### 🆕 Lesson #81 (2026-08-14) — fold into the table at next Brain Health run

`| 81 | 2026-08-14 | Aden pasted an n8n API key straight into chat. I used it only in memory to prove the REST deploy path, never wrote it to disk, told him plainly it was now in the transcript, and asked him to rotate — then verified the old key returned 401 afterwards. Writing it into user-settings.json myself would ALSO have been wrong: HomeBot encrypts that field inside saveSettings via safeStorage, so a script writing the raw JSON stores it in plaintext and quietly defeats the design. | A credential pasted into chat is in the transcript forever. Use it transiently, never persist it, say so, and verify the rotation actually happened rather than trusting the intent. And when an app encrypts a secret at rest, write it through the app's own save path — not the file — or the encryption silently does not happen. | any time a key, token or password appears in conversation |`
